body: Copy-paste bug: this checks `grantType` a second time, with the message for `rawTokenId`. `rawTokenId` is never null-checked, so a null raw id makes `encodeTokenId` produce `onrtac:null`. It should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

Two problems here:
1. This adds an abstract method to a public SPI with no default. Every existing custom `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` in the wild will stop compiling (or fail with `AbstractMethodError` at `postInit`). Consider a `default` implementation.
2. The javadoc says the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters", but `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` hard-codes exactly 2 characters when decoding. A custom grant that follows this javadoc and returns a 3-char shortcut will be encoded fine, e.g. `onrtabc:uuid`. `getTokenContextFromTokenId` will then always throw `Expected length of 6` for those tokens. The javadoc should say exactly 2 characters, and the factory should validate the length (and non-null) at `postInit` and in the lazy refresh path. A `null` shortcut would also NPE inside `ConcurrentHashMap.put` at startup.

Nothing validates the shortcut returned by grant factories: length must be 2, it must be non-null, and it must not collide with the reserved `na`. The duplicate check below uses map sizes, so it only catches collisions indirectly, and a duplicate aborts server startup with an `IllegalStateException`. That is harsh for a third-party grant that happens to reuse e.g. `cc`. The error message should at least name the conflicting grants and shortcut.

Throwing here breaks token issuance for any flow where the `GRANT_TYPE` attribute is set to a value with no registered `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory`. Examples: a grant type disabled via feature flag or provider config, or a custom flow that sets its own value. Before this change, access token creation could not fail for this reason. It would be safer to fall back to `UNKNOWN` (`na`) than to fail the token request with a 500.

`getShouldUseLightweightToken(session)` reads `session.getContext().getClient()`, not the client the token is being issued for. Two consequences:
1. `initToken` now calls it for every access token, even when there are no protocol mappers. Callers such as `KeycloakIdentity` and `PolicyEvaluationService` create access tokens where the context client may be null, which causes an NPE here, or is a different client (the admin console, which has lightweight tokens enabled). In that case the token is wrongly tagged `lt`.
2. Since this PR's stated purpose is to reliably detect lightweight tokens, the value should come from `clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getClient()` plus the session attribute.

The encoded `jti` now depends on state (grant type, lightweight flag, session type) that is resolved at `initToken` time. The lightweight flag can also be set by the `UseLightweightAccessTokenExecutor` client policy through a session attribute. If that executor runs after `initToken`, for example on a token-response event, the `tt` component will disagree with what mappers actually produced. Please verify the ordering, or compute the context after the policies have run.

This matcher is broken in two ways, so it never checks the grant type:
1. `substring(3, 5)` takes the wrong characters. For `onrtac` it returns `ta`; the grant shortcut is at `substring(4, 6)`.
2. The condition is inverted: it returns `false` when the shortcut *matches*.

Because of the wrong offsets, the comparison is never true, so every well-formed id passes. It should be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. Also check that `items[0].length() == 6` first to avoid a `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException`.

The public copy constructor `Context(Context)` was removed from this SPI class. External grant type or token exchange implementations that wrap or copy a `Context` will break. If it has to go, it should be called out as a breaking change. The simpler fix is to keep it and also copy the new `grantType` field.
